The Green Lie: How Electric Companies Are Ripping You Off

When we moved into our new home, we opted into a similar program. We work unusual schedules and are frequently home in the afternoons. They shut off our A/C every day for nearly a week this last month during a heat wave. That wasn't cool. ;)

The program is fine for people who work normal 9-5 type jobs and aren't home most weekday afternoons. For anyone else however, thease programs suck and aren't worth the $5 monthly discount they offer.

Yeah, just buy a decent programmable thermostat and set it up. I'm in south Texas and I'm frequently home all day and I have it setback to 82 until around 4:30pm when it goes to 78 I think. If I'm sitting or just up and milling about its perfectly comfortable. Sometimes I'll adjust it down to 80 during the afternoon if I've been doing a bunch around the house or if I just mowed the yard.

You can usually set a wake up temp, daytime temp, getting home from work temp, and a sleeping temp. The fancier ones (Nest, Honeywell, etc) will sync with your phone and WiFi and offer even more flexibility.

Our program is similar, but doesn't use a thermostat. It's actually a box installed on the outside of the house that the external A/C condenser (I think that's the term) is connected to. They basically control the outlet it's plugged into, bypassing the thermostat completely. Luckily we didn't have any long term contract for it and were able to cancel.

Yeah. I think programs go that route because its cheap and easy to install. The customer doesn't even have to be home, so long as they can get to the unit.

Either way they accomplish the same thing. At least it sounds like people aren't having a terrible time getting out of the program, so that's good.

Had an apartment once and realized they had one of the peak usage devices on my A/C. I work from home so unlike most residence I was home during the day. As soon as I saw it I called the power company and had it removed. They tried to coerce me to stay with an annual $15 credit, told them I think I can make due.

To the power company's credit they came out the next day and removed it.

Yeah, I just don't get how they think saving a couple bucks a month is worth it to any consumer. I'll check the couch cushions, under the seat of the car, and pick up some quarters off the sidewalk to make up for it.

Energy companies want you to get these things so they can shed some load and avoid building out more capacity. They don't care if you save money. They can tack on fees to get that back.

Usually the "discount" or "rebate" they give you is tiny and not worth it. Any homeowner could buy a nicer programmable thermostat than the one they give you and save more than the silly program saves you. Maybe some places with ridiculous rates and serious grid issues might save a bit...SoCal maybe.
